thread.title: Charting a corrective bounce, S&P 500 reclaims 200-day average

author: morningstar.com
title: Charting a corrective bounce, S&P 500 reclaims 200-day average
text:
Though still deeply oversold at current levels, and due a corrective bounce, the group has asserted a bearish longer-term bias, also illustrated on the three-year chart (http://bigcharts.marketwatch.com/advchart/frames/frames.asp?show=&insttype=Fund&symb=XLB&time=10&startdate=1%2F4%2F1999&enddate=10%2F11%2F2018&freq=2&compidx= %3A0&comptemptext=&comp=none&ma=2&maval=20&uf=0&lf=1&lf2=0&lf3=0&type=4&style=320&size=2&timeFrameToggle=false&compareToToggle=false&indicatorsToggle=false&chartStyleToggle=false&state=11&x=36&y=14). Tactically, the breakdown point (57.00) pivots to resistance, and a close higher would strengthen the backdrop.
Similarly, the VanEck Vectors Semiconductor ETF (SMH) has broken down, plunging from trendline support matching the major moving averages.
Tactically, gap resistance (99.30) is followed by the firmer breakdown point (100.80). An eventual close higher would place the brakes on bearish momentum.
More broadly, consider the pending death cross, or bearish 50-day/200-day moving average crossover.
Finally, the SPDR S&P Regional Banking ETF (KRE) has plunged to 11-month lows.
The downdraft punctuates a failed retest of the breakdown point (60.50) and has dovetailed with a bearish 50-day/200-day moving average crossover. Tactically, a close atop near-term resistance (58.60) would mark an early step toward stabilization.
Summing up the sector backdrop
Combined, the October market downdraft has inflicted broadly-based U.S. sub-sector damage. Though a corrective bounce is overdue, and currently underway, an extended basing period would be expected before the next durable leg higher. The quality of the prevailing rally attempt will likely add color.
